The graph shows the number of cell phone subscriptions per capita for the whole world.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
phones <- readr::read_csv("../www/cell-phone-penetration.csv") |>
  dplyr::mutate(rate = subscribers / population)
phones |>
  gf_point(rate ~ year) |>
  gf_line() |>
  gf_labs(y = "subscriptions per capita")
```

Find sensible values for the input and output-scaling parameters using hillside() to represent the relationship between per capita subscriptions and year.

$$ \text{subscriptions}(\text{year})) \equiv A\, \text{hillside}\left(a (\text{year} - b)\right) + B$$

1. What are the input scaling parameters?

```{devoirs_choices}
#| label: choices_cbs.1.wlc
- 'A & a':
    correct: false
- 'B & b':
    correct: false
- 'A & B':
    correct: false
- 'a & b':
    correct: true
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
Q <- devoirs_selection(
  label = "cbs-1-wlc",
  question = "Placeholder for now",
  answers = choices_cbs.1.wlc,
  multiple = FALSE
)
Q(inline = TRUE)
```
